We've all had that Aunt or Uncle that forgot to get you anything for your birthday, christmas, or whatever gift-giving holiday. You open that box all wide-eyed just to see a pair of socks. Fast forward several years and getting socks is awesome!

But what else is like that?
Besides the obvious one like socks, what are some gifts that you would appreciate much more now than you did as a kid?

Toys. No really.

When I was a kid I had lots of toys, almost all of them hand downs. But the only toy which was really bought for me specifically was Knex. I loved the stuff. But after a while I numbed to the gifts so they weren't really exciting any more even though they were welcome and loved.

My dad bought me a box of Knex last year as a gag gift, I'm 23 and long since handed down my collection to a cousin. I always have a few bits on my desk now for messing with, building it up into a tower or a little robot or something useful like a little box for a bit of paper I don't want to forget. It was just a little kindness that got through to me and reignited a childish, personal passion.
I'd rather get the money they were going to spend on the present.

Time. When you're young and all you have is time really, it doesn't really have much value. The fact that your uncle drove two days to see you on Christmas or your dad took the time to build a swingset are just little blips. As you get older, you can see that the time was a bigger sacrifice than the stuff. They gave up time they could have spent on themselves or any other person to spend with you.

Honestly the best gift for me is one that shows the gift giver knows you and what you like. A generic gift like socks is okay, but will never come close to a book by my favorite author, a piece of art that captures who I am, a food or drink that I love.

Those are the gifts that make exchanging gifts magical in my opinion.

Sorry if I didn't exactly answer your question.
Books, clothes of any sort. The older you get the more you realize how stupid you were as a kid.

I recently got this item. I've distilled before, but that was outdoors over a fire. This makes the process so much easier, and safer. I've processed 5 gallons of my apple/honey wine through it, and I'm very happy with the brandy that comes out. Anyone else tried one of these? Pic Manual
Never seen a product like this. Very cool!

It is so simple I would call it elegant. Just a big stainless steal pot that holds a gallon, and a fan/condenser on the top. It makes 750ml of product from that one gallon. It's pretty quiet. Takes about 2.5 hours to process.
I honestly didn't know this was a thing. I'm going to have to spend some time researching what all I can make!

I want to try running some herbs in the pot, maybe with a second run distillation. Cardamom might be nice with the little bit of apple/honey flavor that still remains. I could also see having fun with flowers. Distill twice or three times to get neutral spirits, then flavor with lavender or rose hips. And then of course there is the entire universe of liquors to be mixed up. I think I have gift ideas for all my friends for the next year or so!

Just dump what is left over and rinse. You do have to wait 20 min after unplugging it to open the pot, otherwise you risk steam burns. Oddly enough (to me) there is not a lock or anything keeping the lid on, just a rubber seal. I think that is a safely design though, to keep it from building up dangerous pressures. If something did partially plug up the condenser, the lid can just burp the pressure out.

Huh. That looks pretty clever.

I'm curious about the small size. Seems to me that your run of hearts would be pretty small. How are you making your cuts? Is it fairly easy to get the heads back into the wash to fortify it? What are the tail runs like?

Also, how is disassembling and cleaning it? Stills build up corrosion pretty fast (at my job I disassemble and clean the still every morning. Even the copper column gets nasty after a single day. I run my fingers in there, and there are bits of copper on my fingers.)

It is the essence of simplicity. There are no latches. The top has a rubber seal. The pot is stainless and just needs a rinse. The condenser tubing is also stainless. I've run 7 gallons so far with no sign of corrosion or any buildup. I ran a gallon of my first run back through, and it worked great. No real clue on the percent alcohol, but I'd estimate my first runs are around 30% and my second run is around 50-60%
